stated.text: The app is a small local project-room app titled "Roundtable" (the page shows and is titled Roundtable).
It is served by server.js and runs on Node.js with no npm dependencies (no dependencies in any package.json, no node_modules needed).
The server listens on the port in the PORT environment variable.
When PORT is not set, the server listens on port 3000.
GET / serves the app.
The app has a light, Gemini-like look and feel.
The app starts with one room, named Launch plan.
The Launch plan room is seeded with a realistic conversation.
The seeded conversation contains at least one message from Maya, a person.
The seeded conversation contains at least one message from Theo, a person.
The seeded conversation contains at least one message from Scribe, an agent.
Scribe is clearly identified as a demonstration agent.
The current user is Maya (messages the user sends are authored by Maya).
A region named Conversation contains the messages.
Each message in the Conversation region is an article.
Each message article shows its author.
Each message article shows whether its author is a person or an agent.
Each message article shows its time.
Each message article is accessibly named Message from <author> using its actual author: Message from Maya, Message from Theo or Message from Scribe.
There is a textbox named Message for composing a message.
There is a Send button that sends the composed message.
Pressing Enter in the Message textbox sends the message.
Pressing Shift+Enter in the Message textbox inserts a newline instead of sending.
Whitespace-only text is ignored: sending it (by Send or Enter) adds no message.
A sent message preserves its multiline text (line breaks are kept in the shown message).
Sending clears that draft from the Message textbox.
Sending a message containing @Scribe calls the local POST /api/agent endpoint.
The request to POST /api/agent has the JSON body {"text": <the complete sent text>}.
POST /api/agent is deterministic: it returns exactly {"text": "Demo reply: " followed by the sent text}.
POST /api/agent rejects whitespace-only text with HTTP 400.
POST /api/agent uses no external service.
While awaiting the agent reply, the app shows a working state with role status.
When the agent response fails, the app shows an alert (role alert).
When the agent response fails, the app shows a Retry Scribe button.
Retry Scribe retries the agent reply.
Retrying does not duplicate the person's message.
The URL /?empty=1 starts with an empty conversation.
The empty conversation shows useful guidance.
In the empty conversation, sending still works.
The ?empty=1 fixture control is not a normal UI feature (no visible control offers it).
A visible Use dark appearance button switches the appearance to dark.
After switching to dark, the button becomes Use light appearance.
Use light appearance switches the appearance back to light.
At a 320px browser width, reading and composing stay usable without page-level horizontal scrolling.
At a 390px browser width, reading and composing stay usable without page-level horizontal scrolling.
At a 1440px browser width, reading and composing stay usable without page-level horizontal scrolling.
State can live in the current browser session (no server-side persistence is required).
The state rules are in a module that the app itself uses.
The state rules are covered by node:test tests under test/.
The tests run with node --test.
The delivery has one room and one local agent.
There are no accounts.
There is no file sharing.
There are no canvases.
There are no external services.

unstated.text: How a @Scribe mention is matched: case ("@scribe", "@SCRIBE"), position (start, middle, end of text), punctuation after it ("@Scribe,"), and text where it is part of a longer word ("@Scribes", "me@Scribe.com").
unstated.why: Maya will type the mention in different ways; if a lower-case mention silently gets no reply she thinks the agent is broken, and a false match triggers a reply she did not ask for. The maintainer needs one rule to test.
unstated.probe: Open /. Send "hi @scribe" and wait 3 s; note whether a working state and a Scribe reply appear. Repeat with "@Scribe, can you summarise?", "thanks @Scribes" and "mail me@Scribe.com". Record which ones call POST /api/agent (watch the network panel).
unstated.fine_answers: Case-sensitive exact @Scribe only, or case-insensitive; matching or not matching inside longer words. Any is fine if it is consistent and the case-sensitive form @Scribe at any position with trailing punctuation triggers.

unstated.text: What POST /api/agent does with a body that is not valid JSON, has no text field, has a non-string text (number, null, array), or uses a wrong content type. Only whitespace-only text is said to return 400.
unstated.why: An operator or the next maintainer calling the endpoint by hand needs a clear client error rather than a crash, a hung request or a 500 that kills the server process.
unstated.probe: Start the server. Run: curl -i -X POST localhost:3000/api/agent -d 'not json'; curl -i -X POST localhost:3000/api/agent -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}'; ... -d '{"text":42}'; ... -d '{"text":null}'. Note each status and body, then curl -i localhost:3000/ to confirm the server is still up.
unstated.fine_answers: HTTP 400 with a short JSON error for every malformed case is the plain answer; 415 for wrong content type is also fine. Not fine: a 500 that crashes the server or a request that never answers.

unstated.text: The shape and content type of responses from POST /api/agent, both success (Content-Type header) and the 400 body (empty, plain text, or JSON with an error field).
unstated.why: The front end and any later consumer parse these responses; a 400 with an HTML body or a success without application/json can break parsing.
unstated.probe: curl -i -X POST localhost:3000/api/agent -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"text":"@Scribe hi"}' and note the Content-Type header and body; repeat with '{"text":"   "}'.
unstated.fine_answers: application/json on success is expected; the 400 body may be empty, plain text or JSON with an error message.

unstated.text: How other methods and paths are answered: GET /api/agent, PUT /api/agent, an unknown path like /nope, and whether files outside the app (e.g. /../server.js, /test/) can be fetched.
unstated.why: An operator expects a 404 or 405 rather than the app page on every path, and a maintainer would not want source or arbitrary files served by a hand-written static handler.
unstated.probe: curl -i localhost:3000/api/agent; curl -i -X PUT localhost:3000/api/agent; curl -i localhost:3000/nope; curl -i --path-as-is localhost:3000/../server.js; curl -i --path-as-is 'localhost:3000/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/etc/passwd'. Note statuses and bodies.
unstated.fine_answers: 404 or 405 for unknown routes/methods; serving app assets including the shared state module is fine; serving files outside the project folder is not.

unstated.text: Which network interface the server binds to (localhost only or all interfaces), given the request calls it a local app.
unstated.why: Someone running it on a laptop on shared Wi-Fi may not expect the room to be reachable by others on the network.
unstated.probe: Start the server, run lsof -nP -iTCP:3000 -sTCP:LISTEN (or netstat) and note whether it listens on 127.0.0.1 or *; from another machine try curl http://<host-ip>:3000/.
unstated.fine_answers: Either 127.0.0.1 or all interfaces is acceptable for a local demo; documenting which is enough.

unstated.text: What happens when the PORT is already in use or PORT is not a valid number.
unstated.why: The operator needs a readable message and a non-zero exit, not a silent hang or a stack trace they must decode.
unstated.probe: Start one server on 3000, then run node server.js again; note the output and exit code. Run PORT=abc node server.js and note what it does.
unstated.fine_answers: A clear error and exit, or falling back to the default for an invalid PORT; a raw EADDRINUSE stack trace is tolerable but less useful.

unstated.text: Whether message text is shown as plain text or interpreted as HTML (e.g. a message containing bold, or &).
unstated.why: Maya pasting a code snippet or angle brackets expects to see exactly what she typed; interpreting it as HTML loses text and lets typed content run script.
unstated.probe: Open /, send "bold & @Scribe". Check that the person message and the Scribe reply show the literal characters, no bold, no alert dialog.
unstated.fine_answers: Plain text is the expected answer; a deliberate safe markdown subset would also be fine if it is stated.

unstated.text: What happens if Maya sends another message, or another @Scribe message, while a Scribe reply is still pending: whether the composer stays usable, and in what order replies are placed.
unstated.why: Maya keeps working while Scribe is thinking; replies landing out of order or attached to the wrong message confuse the conversation, and a disabled composer blocks her.
unstated.probe: Throttle the network (devtools Slow 3G) or delay /api/agent. Send "@Scribe first", then immediately "@Scribe second" and "plain note". Wait for all replies and note the order of messages and replies, and whether the working state and Send stayed usable throughout.
unstated.fine_answers: Composer stays usable and replies follow their own messages in send order; or further sends wait/are queued with a visible state. Silently dropping a send is not fine.

unstated.text: Where the Scribe reply appears and how it is shown: as a new message article authored by Scribe, marked as agent, with a time, placed after the person message that mentioned it.
unstated.why: The request states each message article's naming and identity; the reply must follow the same rules or Maya cannot tell what the agent said and when.
unstated.probe: Open /, send "@Scribe summarise". When the reply arrives, inspect the new article: accessible name, author shown, agent identity shown, time shown, text "Demo reply: @Scribe summarise", position right after Maya's message.
unstated.fine_answers: The reply is an article named Message from Scribe with agent identity and a time; exact visual styling is open.

unstated.text: What counts as a failed response and how long the app waits: network error, HTTP 4xx/5xx, a non-JSON body, and a server that never answers (no timeout is stated).
unstated.why: If the server hangs, Maya sees the working state forever with no Retry Scribe; an operator needs failures to surface.
unstated.probe: Stop the server after the page loads and send "@Scribe hi"; note whether an alert and Retry Scribe appear. Restart, intercept /api/agent (devtools request blocking or a local override) to return 500, then to never respond; note what the UI shows after 30 s and 2 min.
unstated.fine_answers: Any timeout from a few seconds to about a minute, or no timeout but a cancel option; network errors and non-2xx both shown as failure.

unstated.text: What the failure alert says, and what happens to the alert and Retry Scribe after a successful retry, after a second failure, and when a later @Scribe message is sent while a failure is shown.
unstated.why: Maya needs to know what failed and that it is fixed; stale alerts or several Retry buttons attached to the wrong messages mislead her.
unstated.probe: Block /api/agent, send "@Scribe one": read the alert text. Click Retry Scribe with the endpoint still blocked: count alerts and Retry buttons. Unblock, click Retry Scribe: check the alert and button disappear and exactly one reply and one Maya message exist. Repeat with two failed mentions in a row and note which message each Retry targets.
unstated.fine_answers: One alert per failed reply or one shared alert; the alert clears on success; retry targets the message whose reply failed.

unstated.text: Whether retry is possible while the retry itself is pending (double clicking Retry Scribe) and whether that can produce two Scribe replies.
unstated.why: A duplicate agent reply is the agent-side twin of the duplicate person message the request forbids.
unstated.probe: Throttle the network, block /api/agent, send "@Scribe once", unblock, double-click Retry Scribe quickly. Count Scribe replies after it settles.
unstated.fine_answers: Retry disabled or hidden while pending, or a guard ignoring a second click; exactly one reply results.

unstated.text: Whether the conversation, sent messages, failure state and appearance survive a page reload or a new tab, given state "can live in the current browser session".
unstated.why: Maya who reloads by accident may expect her messages to stay; a tester expects a predictable reset. The maintainer must know which store is used.
unstated.probe: Open /, send "keep me", switch to dark appearance, reload. Note whether the message and dark appearance remain. Open / in a new tab and in a private window and note the same.
unstated.fine_answers: Kept via sessionStorage for the tab, or reset on reload to the seed; either if consistent. Persisting across browser restarts is also fine.

unstated.text: How /?empty=1 interacts with saved session state and with navigating back to /: whether an empty fixture overwrites the seeded room's stored state, and whether stored messages override the empty start.
unstated.why: A tester switching between / and /?empty=1 needs each URL to start as described; leaking state between them makes the fixture unreliable.
unstated.probe: Open /, send "seeded extra". Open /?empty=1 in the same tab: is the conversation empty with guidance? Send "from empty". Go to / again: what messages are shown? Reload /?empty=1: empty again or containing "from empty"?
unstated.fine_answers: ?empty=1 always starts empty and does not disturb the seeded room's state; or it starts empty once and then keeps its own session state. Showing seeded messages under ?empty=1 is not fine.

unstated.text: What the empty-state guidance says and whether it disappears once the first message is sent.
unstated.why: "Useful guidance" should tell Maya how to start and how to call Scribe; guidance left on top of a real conversation is clutter.
unstated.probe: Open /?empty=1, read the guidance text (does it mention typing a message and @Scribe?). Send "hello". Check the guidance is gone or reduced and the message shows as an article.
unstated.fine_answers: Any guidance that explains composing and mentioning @Scribe; removed or kept small after the first message.

unstated.text: The initial appearance: always light, or following the system's prefers-color-scheme; and whether the button label matches when the system is dark.
unstated.why: A user with a dark system theme may get dark by default; the button must then say Use light appearance, or the label lies.
unstated.probe: Emulate prefers-color-scheme: dark in devtools, open /. Note the appearance and the button's label. Repeat with light.
unstated.fine_answers: Always start light (matches "light, Gemini-like look") or follow the system with a correct label.

unstated.text: Whether the dark appearance keeps text and controls readable (contrast of messages, timestamps, identity badges, alert, focus outline).
unstated.why: A dark mode with low-contrast timestamps or invisible focus rings makes reading and composing unusable for some users.
unstated.probe: Switch to dark, run an accessibility contrast check (e.g. Lighthouse or axe) on the page, and tab through Message, Send, appearance toggle and Retry Scribe checking the focus indicator is visible.
unstated.fine_answers: WCAG AA contrast for text is the plain target; exact palette is open.

unstated.text: How very long unbroken text (a long URL or a 300-character word) and very long messages wrap at 320px, and whether the message list scrolls inside its region.
unstated.why: The no-horizontal-scroll rule is most often broken by a long link pasted into a message, which Maya will do in a project room.
unstated.probe: Set the viewport to 320px wide, send "https://example.com/" followed by 300 letters without spaces, and a 40-line message. Check document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= 320 and the full text is readable by wrapping or scrolling within the message.
unstated.fine_answers: Breaking long words, or scrolling inside the message bubble; no page-level horizontal scroll.

unstated.text: Whether the view scrolls to the newest message after sending and after a Scribe reply arrives, and whether focus returns to the Message textbox after sending.
unstated.why: In a long conversation Maya should see what she just sent and the reply without hunting, and keep typing without clicking back into the box.
unstated.probe: Open /, send ten messages so the Conversation overflows, scroll up, then send "@Scribe latest". Note whether the view shows the new message and the reply, and where keyboard focus is (document.activeElement).
unstated.fine_answers: Auto-scroll on own send and on reply (perhaps only when already near the bottom); focus stays on or returns to the textbox.

unstated.text: Whether new messages and the Scribe reply are announced to screen-reader users (live region), beyond the working state's role status.
unstated.why: A screen-reader user hears that Scribe is working but may not learn the reply has arrived.
unstated.probe: With VoiceOver or NVDA on, send "@Scribe hi" and listen: is the working state announced, and then the reply or its arrival? Or inspect the DOM for aria-live on the conversation or a status update on completion.
unstated.fine_answers: A polite live announcement of the reply, or the status region saying the reply arrived; either works.

unstated.text: How message times are shown: format, time zone, the times given to the seeded messages (fixed or relative to now), and whether they carry a machine-readable datetime.
unstated.why: A realistic seed with times in the future or in an odd format reads as broken; a maintainer testing time rules needs predictable values.
unstated.probe: Open / and read each seeded message's time; inspect for a <time datetime> element. Send a message and compare its time with the clock. Change the OS time zone, reload, compare.
unstated.fine_answers: Local clock time (e.g. 10:42 AM) or relative ("2 min ago"); seeded times before the current user's new messages.

unstated.text: Whether sending is limited in length or the endpoint limits the request body size.
unstated.why: A pasted huge text could freeze the page or make the server buffer an unbounded body; an operator would want a known ceiling.
unstated.probe: Send a 200,000-character message containing @Scribe and note whether the UI stays responsive and the reply arrives. curl -X POST localhost:3000/api/agent with a 50 MB JSON body and note status and server memory.
unstated.fine_answers: No limit for a local demo is acceptable if large but sane messages work; a stated limit with a clear message (e.g. 413) is also fine.

unstated.text: Whether leading/trailing whitespace of a non-empty message is trimmed before display and before being sent to the agent (the agent echoes "the complete sent text").
unstated.why: The exact echo is a stated contract, so the maintainer must know whether "  @Scribe hi  \n" is sent as typed or trimmed; Maya may notice stray blank lines.
unstated.probe: Type "  @Scribe hi" then Shift+Enter twice, then Send. Inspect the POST /api/agent request body and the shown person message and reply for leading spaces and trailing newlines.
unstated.fine_answers: Sent exactly as typed, or trimmed in both the message and the request; the shown message and the request text must match.

unstated.text: Behaviour of Enter during text composition with an IME (Japanese, Chinese input) and on mobile virtual keyboards.
unstated.why: Enter that confirms an IME candidate must not send a half-composed message; on a phone at 390px there is no Shift key, so how a newline is entered matters.
unstated.probe: Enable a Japanese IME, type "konnichiha" in Message, press Enter to confirm the candidate; check nothing was sent. On a mobile emulator at 390px, check whether the return key sends or inserts a newline.
unstated.fine_answers: Enter during composition (isComposing) does not send; on mobile, the return key sending or inserting a newline are both acceptable.

unstated.text: Whether the Send button is disabled or still active when the draft is empty or whitespace-only.
unstated.why: Users need to see why nothing happened; the request only says such text is ignored.
unstated.probe: Open /, leave Message empty, then type three spaces; check the Send button's disabled state and click it; confirm no message is added and no error appears.
unstated.fine_answers: Disabled while empty, or enabled and ignoring the click; both fine as long as nothing is sent.

unstated.text: How the tests are run by a maintainer (an npm test script or just node --test) and which Node.js version is needed.
unstated.why: The next maintainer needs to know the one command and the minimum Node version (node:test and node --test discovery differ across versions).
unstated.probe: In the project folder, run node --test and npm test; note results. Check package.json for scripts and engines and the README for run instructions.
unstated.fine_answers: node --test alone, or an npm test script wrapping it; a README line naming the command and a working Node version.

unstated.text: Whether the seeded conversation reads as a realistic Launch plan discussion, and whether Scribe's seeded message makes its demonstration nature clear (label or badge visible in the message, not only in hidden text).
unstated.why: The customer will demo this; placeholder text or an agent that looks like a person undermines it.
unstated.probe: Open / and read the seed: check the messages discuss a launch plan coherently and that Scribe's article shows a visible label such as Demo agent.
unstated.fine_answers: Any coherent launch-planning exchange; any visible marker (badge, "demo agent" label) for Scribe.
